Here’s a mix of classic chills, modern scares, psychological thrillers, supernatural tales, and even some underrated gems—so there’s something for almost every kind of horror fan!

| # | Title (Year) | Sub‑genre / Notable Twist |
|---|--------------|---------------------------|
| **1** | *Psycho* (1960) | Classic slasher + iconic shower scene; Hitchcock at his best. |
| **2** | *Nightmare on Elm Street* (1984) | Dream‑based terror – Freddy Krueger brings nightmares into reality. |
| **3** | *The Shining* (1980) | Psychological horror set in an isolated hotel; Jack Nicholson delivers a chilling performance. |
| **4** | *Get Out* (2017) | Social satire meets body‑horror; clever use of symbolism. |
| **5** | *Hereditary* (2018) | Family trauma turned supernatural dread; intense atmosphere. |
| **6** | *Midsommar* (2019) | Daylight horror – unsettling folk rituals in Sweden. |
| **7** | *It Follows* (2014) | A curse passed through sexual contact; creepy synth score amplifies tension. |
| **8** | *A Quiet Place* (2018) | Silence as survival strategy against sound‑sensing monsters. |
| **9** | *The Babadook* (2014) | Supernatural entity emerges from a children’s book; explores grief & motherhood. |
| **10** | *Suspiria* (1977) | Giallo style dance academy turns deadly; vivid color palette. |

### Underrated Picks Worth Watching  
| # | Title (Year) | Why It Stands Out |
|---|--------------|--------------------|
| **11** | *Session 9* (2001) | An abandoned asylum becomes claustrophobic nightmare; strong atmospheric build-up. |
| **12** | *The Others* (2001) | Ghost story with a twist; Nicole Kidman leads a tense family drama. |
| **13** | *The Witch* (2015) | Slow burn Puritan-era paranoia; meticulous period detail creates unease. |
| **14** | *Kill List* (2011) | Starts as hit‑men thriller then morphs into cult horror; keeps viewers guessing. |
| **15** | *Pontypool* (2008) | Viral outbreak via radio broadcast; unique take on zombie lore. |

---

#### Quick Tips If You’re New to Horror:
1. **Start With Classics:** Films like *Halloween*, *Friday the 13th*, and *Alien* lay foundational tropes.  
2. **Mix Up Genres:** Try both slashers (*Scream*) and psychological horrors (*Black Swan*) to see what resonates most.  
3. **Watch In Groups:** Some scenes work better when shared—especially if they involve jump scares!  

Enjoy your frightful marathon—and remember: keep the lights off… but don’t forget the popcorn!
